l.e: •Gusaba abanyeshuri kuririmba, kubyina no gukoma amashyi.

l.t: Interuro mboneza mvugo n’interuro nyobyamvugo (Amasah a 2)
l.o:
•Gutanduka nya neza interuro nyobyamvug n’interuro mbonezamv ugo;
•Gukoresha neza, mu mvugo no mu nyandiko, interuro mbonezamu go zigaragaza neza igihe igikorwa cyakorewe n’isanisha riboneye.
l.c:
•Gusoban ura inshoza y'interuro mboneza mvug n'interuro nyobyamv ugo;
•Gukoresha mu mvug no mu nyandiko, interuro mboneza mvugo.
l.e: •Gukora imyitozo iri mu gitabo cyabo

l.o: •Kuvuga ashize amanga inkuru cyangwa umuvugo yasomye.
l.c: •Kubara inkuru no gutondag ura umuvugo basomye.
l.a: •Gusaba abanyeshuri, umwumwe, gusubiramo inkuru, ikinamico cyangwa umuvugo basomye ashyize amanga.

•Igitabo cy’umunyeshuri
•Igitabo cy’umwarimu;
•Umwarimu ashaka n’izindi mfashanyigisho zifatika n’izidafatika zijyanye n’iri
somo ziboneka aho ishuri riherereye.
l.e: •Gusubira mo inkuru, ikinamico cyangwa umuvugo basomye.

l.c: •Kuririmba bashize amanga.

l.e:
•Kuririmba indirimbo 'Turate Rwanda yacu'' ku giti cyabo
no gukora akarasisi.

l.t: Ubumen yi ngiro (Guhanga indirimbo no kuyiririmba)
l.o: •Guhanga neza indirimbo no kuyiririmba imbere ya bagenzi be adategwa.
l.c: •Guhanga indirimbo no Kuririmba .
l.a:
•Gusaba abanyeshuri kongera gusoma indirimbo ''Turate Rwanda'' kubasaba kunoza umukoro bari bahawe wo guhanga indirimbo;
•Gusaba buri munyeshuri ku giti ke, kujya imbere ya bagenzi be maze akabaririmbira indirimbo yahanze.
l.e: •Buri munyeshuri kujya imbere akaririmba mu mutwe, indirimbo ye yahanze atayisoma.

l.t: Ibikorwa byo gusoma: Gusoma ibitabo mu isomero
l.o: •Gukina inkuru cyangwa ikinamico
l.c: •Kuvuga ashize amanga kandi yigana abanyaru buga bo mu nkuru yasomye cyangwa abakinan ku ru bo mu ikinamico yafashe mu mutwe.
l.a: •Kujyana abanyeshuri mu isomer bagahitamo igitabo bashaka gusoma nyuma bakaza kubwira bagenzi babo ibyo basomye.
l.e: •Gukina inkuru basomye cyangwa gukina ikinamico bafashe mu mutwe.

l.t: Ubumen yi ngiro (Kungura na ibitekerezo) Isuzuma bushobo zi risoza umutw e wa gatanu. (Amasah a 2)
l.o:
•Gusoma no gusubiza neza ibibazo ijyanye no gusesengura umwandiko.
•Gusuzuma niba intego z'ibyigwa muri uyu mutwe zaragezweho hashingiwe ku bushobozi bw' ingenzi bugamijwe.
l.c:
•Gusoma umwandiko no gusubiza ibibazo byo guseseng ura umwandiko.
•Ibibazo by'isuzum a.
l.a:
•Kubaza abanyeshuri ibibazo bituma biyibutsa umwandiko baheruka kwika;
•Gusaba abanyeshuri mu matsinda gukora ibibazo byo gusesesngura umwandiko.
•Guha abanyeshuri amabwiriza y'isuzuma.
•Kubasaba gukora isuzuma no gufasha abafite imbogamizi.
•Nyuma y'isuzuma, gutanga ubujyanama ngarukirane.
l.e:
•Kubaza abanyeshuri ibindi bibazo ku mwandiko basomye kugira ngo umenye ko bawumvise koko.
•Gukora isuzuma risoza umutwe.

l.e: •Buri wese ku giti ke gukora Imyitozo iri mu gitabo cyabo.

l.o:

•Gufasha abagaragaje ubushobozi buke kuzamura urwego ku masomo batumvise neza, no kubatera umwete mu byo biga.
•Gufasha abafite ubushozi buhagije kubwongera .
l.c:
•Gutega amatwi inkuru no gutanga ibitekerezo ku nkuru.
•Imyitozo nzamurab ushobozi na nyagurab ushobozi yateguwe.
l.e:
•Gusubiza neza ibibazo ku nkuru yasomewe.
•Gukora imyitozo nzamurab ushobozi na nyagurabu shobozi yateguwe.

•Igitabo cy’umunyeshuri
•Igitabo cy’umwarimu;

aho ishuri riherereye.

•Gusoma Umwandiko.
•Iby'ingen zi bikubiye mu mwandiko umunyeshuri yisomeye n'inyungu ramagam bo.

•Gusaba abanyeshuri gushaka ibisobanuro by’ amagambo batari basobanukiwe.
l.e: •Gusaba abanyeshuri gukora umwitozo uri mu bitabo byabo wo gukoresha amagambo mu nteruro.

l.e: •Kubaza abanyeshuri ibindi bibazo ku mwandiko basomye kugira ngo umenye ko bawumvise koko.

l.o: Give the meaning of terms: pre-colonial period, pre-colonial Rwanda, traditional Rwanda, colonisation, colonial Rwanda. Explain the characteristics of traditional Rwanda
l.c:
Pre-colonial period: the time in history before a country or region was taken over or controlled by foreign powers. Pre-colonial Rwanda: the history of Rwanda before European colonisers arrived, when the country was ruled by its own kings (Abami) and organised according to its traditional social, political, economic, and cultural systems. Traditional Rwanda: Rwanda as it was in the
past, with its customs, culture, governance by kings, social organisation (such as clans), and traditional practices before modern or foreign influence. Characteristics of traditional Rwanda
• Rwanda was led by a king (Umwami) who lived in a palace.
• Cows were very important and used as gifts and in ceremonies.
• Families lived in round grass huts called urugo.
• People told stories and danced, especially around fires in the evenings.
• Most people were farmers growing
l.a:
• Guide pupils to understand what is meant by pre-colonial Rwanda.
• Put pupils in groups talk about what did people wear in pre-colonial Rwanda?
• Facilitate the group discussions pupils talk about meaning of Colonization.
• Together with the pupils we talk about
the king and his kingdom.

• Military chiefs led the army to protect and expand the Kingdom...

of chiefs (Military, Land, and Cattle).
• Group work: Pupils are divided into three groups. Each group is assigned one type of chief. They discuss what they think that the chief did.
• Role-play: Each group acts out what their chief did to help the king.

Main economic activities in pre-colonial Rwanda were farming, cattle keeping, hunting, fishing, and craft making...
• Crop cultivation: Farmers grew important crops like millet, beans, bananas, sorghum, and sweet potatoes.
• Livestock: Cattle were very valuable, used for milk, meat, and as a form
of payment in social exchanges like dowries.
• Markets: Regular markets allowed people to buy and sell goods locally and with nearby regions.
• Hunting and gathering: People hunted animals and gathered wild foods to add to their diet.
l.a:
In small groups, pupils discuss economic activities in pre-colonial Rwanda (e.g. farming, cattle keeping, hunting, bartering) and economic activities in modern Rwanda (e.g. office work, using
money, selling goods, banks, factories), then presents their findings.
l.m: • Videos, photos and pictures.
l.e:
Identify the main economic activities in pre-colonial Rwanda (e.g. farming, cattle keeping, hunting, fishing, and craft making) and explain how Rwanda was economically organized in the pre-colonial period.
through oral and written questions and answers.

l.t: Differences between traditional and modern trade
l.o: Compare traditional and modern trade
l.c:
In traditional trade:
• Local trade: Happened within nearby communities.
• Barter system: Goods were exchanged without money (e.g., sorghum for beans).
• Traded goods: Included food, cattle, tools, pots, clothes, fish, and honey.
l.a: In groups discuss traditional and modern trade, then make a presentation to the class followed by questions and answers. Role-play in class how barter trade was carried out in pre-colonial Rwanda.
